concepts.name: Uniformly Accelerated Motion
concepts.definition: Motion in a straight line with constant acceleration, where velocity changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals.
concepts.conditions: Acceleration vector is constant in magnitude and direction along the motion axis.

concepts.name: Free Fall Under Gravity
concepts.definition: Vertical motion of an object solely under the influence of Earth gravity, neglecting air resistance.
concepts.conditions: Near Earth surface, downward acceleration magnitude is g = 9.8 m/s^2 or 10 m/s^2.

concepts.name: Stopping Distance & Reaction Time
concepts.definition: Distance traversed by a vehicle between driver reaction initiation and complete halt under braking retardation.
concepts.conditions: Final velocity v = 0 under constant braking acceleration a = -a_brake.

problem_patterns.title: Linear Kinematics with Constant Acceleration
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Given initial velocity and acceleration or time, determine final velocity or displacement using kinematic equations
problem_patterns.governing_method: Identify knowns (u, v, a, s, t), select kinematic equation eliminating unknown, solve algebraically, verify SI units
decision_points: Set coordinate origin and sign convention
Choose equation containing knowns and target variable
common_traps: Confusing average speed with instantaneous speed
Incorrect sign convention for acceleration opposing motion

problem_patterns.title: Vertical Projectile Motion Under Gravity
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Object thrown vertically upward reaches max height with v = 0 and falls back under constant downward gravity g
problem_patterns.governing_method: Establish upward positive axis with a = -g, compute max height H = u^2/(2g) and time of flight T = 2u/g
decision_points: Account for downward acceleration g = 10 m/s^2
Utilize symmetry of ascent and descent durations
common_traps: Assuming acceleration is zero at highest point
Forgetting net displacement is zero upon returning to launch height

source_problems.statement: A vehicle accelerates uniformly from rest at a rate of 2.5 m/s^2 for 8 s. It then travels at constant speed for 10 s. What is the total distance covered by the vehicle?
source_solution_steps: Phase 1: Acceleration from rest (u = 0, a = 2.5 m/s^2, t1 = 8 s). s1 = 0.5 * a * t1^2 = 0.5 * 2.5 * 64 = 80 m.
Speed attained: v = u + a * t1 = 0 + 2.5 * 8 = 20 m/s.
Phase 2: Constant speed (v = 20 m/s, t2 = 10 s). s2 = v * t2 = 20 * 10 = 200 m.
Total distance: s = s1 + s2 = 80 + 200 = 280 m.

source_problems.statement: A car moving with an initial speed of 30 m/s is brought to rest with uniform retardation in 6 s. The distance traversed by the car during this retardation period is:
source_solution_steps: Initial speed u = 30 m/s, final speed v = 0, time t = 6 s.

source_problems.statement: A stone is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed of 20 m/s from the top of a tower of height 25 m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the total time taken by the stone to reach the ground is:
source_solution_steps: Choose upward as positive axis. Position of release y0 = 0, ground is at y = -25 m.
Initial velocity u = +20 m/s, acceleration a = -g = -10 m/s^2.
Kinematic equation: y = ut + 0.5 * a * t^2 => -25 = 20t - 5t^2.
Factorize: (t - 5)(t + 1) = 0. Since time t > 0, t = 5 s.

source_problems.statement: A ball dropped from the top of a building takes 3 s to reach the ground. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the height of the building and the speed with which it strikes the ground are respectively:
source_solution_steps: Dropped from rest: u = 0, t = 3 s, g = 10 m/s^2.
Final speed v = g * t = 10 * 3 = 30 m/s.
